newsitem.title: TAIWAN: SHINKONG PLANS $25 MLN CHINA PROJECT.
newsitem.headline: SHINKONG PLANS $25 MLN CHINA PROJECT.

text.p: Taiwan's textile maker Shinkong Synthetic Fribres said on Monday it planned to invest US$25 million to set up a chemical fibre plant in China.
Shinkong Fibres, a leading Taiwan yarn and fibre-maker, announced the project despite new China-Taiwan friction sparked by Beijing's successful diplomatic courtship of South Africa.

"For textile companies like us, the main market is now in mainland China," Shinkong finance manager Ku Chao-nan said by telephone. "It's better to have our own production line there in order to compete with others."
Ku said the plant would be built in Hangzou pending approval from the Taiwan government's Investment Commision, which oversees Taiwan investment in the rival mainland.
If approved, Shinkong would be the second Taiwan company to set up a chemical fibre plant on the mainland after Far Eastern Textiles , Ku said.
It is unclear whether a freeze on China economic initiatives set by Taiwan would make approvals harder to obtain.
Taiwan imposed a freeze to retaliate for China's strong and fruitful push to establish formal ties with South Africa.
South Africa, one of only 30 states recognising Taiwan's exiled Republic of China, stunned the island last week by vowing to sever ties with Taipei in favour of Beijing by 1998.

Taiwan has banned all direct official contact with China after a civil war split them in 1949. All investments in China must be government approved and routed indirectly through Hong Kong or other third places.
Despite the ban, indirect commerce has flourished since a late 1980s political thaw and some 30,000 Taiwa companies now have poured more than US$20 billion into the mainland.
Worried that Taiwan may become over-dependent on the mainlaind for investment, President Lee Tung-hui has said the island needed to review its policy of targeting China as its main market.
